title: The Quiet Drummer
moral: Everyone has something valuable to give. Kindness means noticing quiet people and helping them shine.

pages.text:
The annual day practice had made Class Four very noisy.

Some children were dancing. Some were singing. Some were walking around with paper flowers, trying not to bend them.

Kabir stood near the back, counting loudly.

"One, two, three, mango!"

Everyone stopped.

"It is four," said Tara.

Kabir looked serious. "Mango keeps me alert."

Everyone laughed.

Tara was the lead dancer. She liked being in the front because she knew all the steps. But every time the music started, something went wrong.

The group moved too fast. Then too slow. Then two children turned left while everyone else turned right.

Miss Renu sighed. "We need someone to keep the beat."

At the back of the room sat Aahil. He was quiet and usually avoided the stage. He tapped his fingers softly on an empty water can.

Tap-tap. Tap-tap-tap.

The sound was steady.

Tara noticed first.

"Can you do that while we dance?" she asked.

Aahil looked surprised. "Me?"

"Yes," Tara said. "You are keeping the beat better than the speaker."

Aahil smiled a little.

The next time the music played, Aahil sat near the side and tapped the can gently. The dancers followed the rhythm.

No one bumped into anyone. Even Kabir remembered four.

After practice, Miss Renu said, "Much better!"

On annual day, Tara stood in front. The lights were bright. The hall was full.

For one second, she felt nervous.

Then she heard it.

Tap-tap. Tap-tap-tap.

Aahil was sitting near the curtain with the water can, steady as a little drum.

Tara smiled and began.

The dance went perfectly.

Everyone clapped for the dancers. Tara bowed, then turned and pointed toward Aahil.

"He helped us keep the beat," she said.

The clapping grew louder.

Aahil's face turned red, but his smile was big.

Later, Kabir whispered, "Next year, I will also play water bottle."

Tara laughed.

Aahil held the empty can like a prize. It was not a real drum. But that day, it had made the whole class move together.
